note: At an ungated railroad crossing with no flashing signals, you must slow, look, and listen for trains and be ready to stop. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough room for your entire vehicle to clear all tracks without stopping on them.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:You should come to a complete stop,c:You should merge into a lane in the arrow's direction
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may make the turn, but it is not protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians, and only turn when there is a safe gap.

question: If a police officer asks you to take a chemical alcohol test, what must you do?
options: a:Do not have to take the test if you can prove that you weren’t drinking,b:Do not have to take the test if you have not violated any traffic rule.,c:Must take the test or risk losing your license.
note: Under implied consent laws, by driving you agree to take a chemical test (breath, blood, or urine) when an officer lawfully requests it. You may refuse, but refusal typically results in automatic license suspension or revocation, even if you were not drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which of these should you NOT fail to do?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intention.,c:Check over your shoulder for other vehicles in your blind spot.,d:Ignore traffic beside you if mirrors look clear.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never ignore traffic beside you just because your mirrors look clear; a vehicle can be hidden in your blind spot.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Firmly slam on the brakes.,d:Shift into neutral.
note: On a slippery road, ease off the accelerator first so the vehicle can slow down gradually. If you need to brake, do so gently and steadily to avoid skidding; sudden or hard braking can cause loss of control.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It decreases BAC quickly.,b:It cancels the effects of alcohol.,c:It has no effect on BAC and does not sober you up.,d:It speeds up how fast your body metabolizes alcohol.
note: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you sober. It may make you feel more awake, but only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC.

question: Which color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red lines.,b:White lines.,c:Yellow lines.,d:Blue lines.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and usually mark the right edge of the roadway. Broken white lines may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: Why must you be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see,b:They rarely use headlights,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled than car drivers
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be easily hidden in blind spots or behind other vehicles, making them harder to see and judge for speed and distance. Drivers must look carefully for motorcycles, especially when changing lanes or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign,b:The reduced speed applies only after the next sign,c:You have plenty of distance to slow down before the reduced zone
note: When you see a sign showing a reduced speed limit, that new speed limit generally begins at the sign. You must be at or below the posted speed as you reach the sign, not some distance after it.

question: How is an arrogant driver typically described?
options: a:Someone purposely in a hurry and competing with other traffic.,b:A driver who shows little respect for traffic laws and others.,c:A driver you should try to avoid while driving.,d:All of the above.
note: An arrogant driver often drives aggressively, rushes, competes with other traffic, and shows little respect for traffic laws or other road users. It is safest to stay away from such drivers and avoid reacting to their behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so you can merge smoothly with traffic. Always signal and yield to vehicles already on the freeway; they have the right-of-way. Enter at or near the speed of traffic when it is safe to do so.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping,b:That you are making a turn,c:That your emergency brake is engaged
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions. Make sure your brake lights work properly at all times.

question: Which device increases crash risk when used by drivers?
options: a:CD player.,b:Radio.,c:Cell phone.,d:Hands-free intercom.
note: Cell phone use, including talking, texting, or browsing, is one of the most dangerous driver distractions. It takes your eyes, mind, and sometimes hands away from driving, greatly increasing crash risk, even when using hands-free features.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for others to know your plans.,b:Just as you begin to change lanes.,c:After you change lanes.,d:Signal only if traffic is heavy.
note: Always signal well in advance of changing lanes or passing so other drivers have time to see your signal and understand what you plan to do. The signal must be on before you start moving into another lane, not during or after the maneuver.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.,b:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:Decreasing your chances of an accident.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your reaction time, which lowers your ability to focus on driving and increases crash risk. While extreme fatigue can cause drowsiness, ordinary stress by itself does not typically make you fall asleep at the wheel.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, turn on your four‑way (hazard) flashers immediately so other drivers can see that your vehicle is disabled. If it is safe, move as far off the roadway as possible, signal and exit carefully, and you may raise your hood to show that the vehicle is disabled.

question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic moves.,b:Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,d:Back up to make room.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and you would be forced to stop in the intersection, stay behind the stop line or crosswalk and wait until there is enough space to drive all the way through.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Proceed.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.,d:Stop immediately at the line.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: When approaching railroad tracks you should:
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop,b:Speed up to cross before any gate comes down,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains or warning signals. Be prepared to stop if a train is coming or if signals are activated. Never speed up to beat a train and never drive around or under a lowered gate.

question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use parking lights.
note: In rain, always use low‑beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off rain, fog, or snow and can make it harder for you and other drivers to see. Parking lights alone are not sufficient while driving.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Using proper turn signals.,c:Obeying posted speed limits.,d:All of the above.
note: Allowing extra travel time, using proper turn signals, and obeying posted speed limits all help reduce stress and prevent aggressive driving. Planning ahead so you are not rushed, signaling early and clearly, and driving at legal speeds make you more predictable and courteous, which lowers the chance of conflicts with other drivers.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and you are sure no other train is coming before you proceed, even if warning devices are not working.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When flashing red signals and/or gates are present and operating.,b:When it is controlled by a stop sign.,c:When directed to do so by a flagger.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time warning devices are activated, a stop sign controls the crossing, or a flagger directs you to stop. Flashing red lights, lowered gates, a posted stop sign, or instructions from a flagger all require you to come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is clearly safe.

question: What factor strongly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Signal lights.,b:The condition of the road surface.,c:The time of day.,d:The color of your vehicle.
note: The condition of the road surface has a major effect on how quickly you can stop. Wet, icy, gravel, or uneven pavement greatly increases stopping distance, so you must slow down and increase following distance when road conditions are poor.

question: All vehicle headlights must be working and properly aimed:
options: a:At all times,b:Only when driving in a city,c:Only on freeways
note: Headlights are required equipment and must be in working order and properly aimed whenever the vehicle is operated. Properly adjusted headlights help you see the road and allow others to see you, especially at night or in poor visibility.

question: When should safety belts be worn?
options: a:Should be worn only when traveling at high speeds.,b:Should be worn at all times when driving or riding in a vehicle.,c:Should be worn loosely.
note: Safety belts should be worn by drivers and passengers at all times while the vehicle is moving. Wearing them correctly and snugly across the lap and shoulder greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should end up in which lane?
options: a:The lane nearest to the left side of the one-way street (left lane),b:The right lane of the street,c:The center of the street
note: When turning left from a two‑way street onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you on the one‑way street, which is the left lane. Turning into the nearest appropriate lane helps prevent conflicts with other traffic and is required by most state laws.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow line in the center of the road separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross this line to pass another vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,c:Stop with part of your vehicle on the roadway.,d:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop if necessary and yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians and all vehicles already on the roadway. Only enter when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: On an undivided roadway, when may you pass a school bus?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when the bus's red warning lights are flashing.,c:When the bus's red warning lights are not flashing.,d:Only if the bus is stopped to let students off on the opposite side.
note: On an undivided roadway, you must stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended, regardless of your direction of travel. You may proceed or pass only when the red lights are off and the stop arm is retracted, and only if it is otherwise safe and legal.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:If you lose control and need to alert others,b:When passing another car for routine reasons,c:To express anger
note: Use your horn only to warn others of a safety problem, such as when you lose control, another driver is about to hit you, or a pedestrian may not see you. Do not use the horn to express anger, to scare others, or for routine passing when there is no immediate danger.

question: If stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must produce:
options: a:Only proof of insurance,b:Their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance,c:Only their license
note: During a traffic stop, you must be prepared to show the officer your valid driver license, the vehicle’s registration, and proof of financial responsibility (insurance). These documents show that you are legally allowed to drive and that the vehicle is properly registered and insured.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass,b:Retaliate by tailgating them,c:Cut them off to slow them down
note: When dealing with an aggressive driver, focus on safety and avoiding conflict. Do not make eye contact or respond with gestures, slow down if needed, and create space so they can pass. Retaliating or trying to block them increases the risk of a crash and can escalate road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but no stop line or crosswalk is painted, where should you stop?
options: a:You are not required to stop.,b:Stop at a point nearest the roadway where you can safely see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.,c:Stop in the intersection to get a better view.,d:Stop where you can see at least 500 feet in both directions.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must still stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic, but without moving into the intersection itself. This lets you check for cross traffic while staying out of the flow of vehicles.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: When towing, where should the trailer's safety chain be attached on the towing vehicle?
options: a:To the frame of the towing vehicle,b:To the vehicle's bumper,c:To the trailer's hitch only
note: Safety chains are a backup connection between the trailer and the towing vehicle. They should be attached to solid points on the towing vehicle’s frame or to frame-mounted hitch components, not just to a bumper, which can tear off in a crash. Crossing the chains under the tongue also helps catch it if the hitch fails.

question: What should you do before driving into an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your route in advance,b:Depend entirely on road signs while driving,c:Have only a general idea of the destination
note: Before driving into an unfamiliar area, you should plan your route so you know the main roads, turns, and exits. This reduces last‑second lane changes and distractions from constantly searching for signs or directions while driving.

question: A good defensive driver:
options: a:Anticipates actions of other drivers and watches for hazards,b:Drives slowly at all times,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions
note: A good defensive driver stays alert, scans the road ahead, and anticipates what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do. They adjust speed and position to road, traffic, and weather conditions instead of driving at one speed all the time.

question: When must you stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is stopped in your lane.,b:Only if you see children outside the bus.,c:When its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.,d:Never, if you are on the opposite side of the road.
note: On a two‑lane highway, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, even if you do not immediately see children.

question: Which factors affect your vehicle's braking distance?
options: a:The vehicle's speed.,b:Condition of brakes and tires.,c:Condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed and is also affected by how well your brakes work, the condition and tread of your tires, and the road surface (wet, icy, gravel, or dry pavement). Poor brakes, worn tires, or slippery pavement all make your vehicle take longer to stop.

question: What is the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:An orange reflective triangle bordered in red,b:A rectangular red sign,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border. It is used on vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less, warning faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your radio.,b:Your rearview mirror.,c:The steering wheel.,d:Your seat.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and see clearly over the steering wheel. Once your seating position is correct, adjust mirrors and the steering wheel to match that position.

question: Combining drugs with alcohol will:
options: a:Increase your risk of causing a crash,b:Reduce alcohol's effect on driving,c:Be no more dangerous than alcohol alone
note: Mixing alcohol with any drugs—illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter—can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. This combination makes a crash much more likely than using alcohol alone.

question: An \End school zone\" sign notifies drivers that:"
options: a:The reduced school zone speed limit has ended,b:A 20 mph limit begins,c:You are entering a school area
note: An “End school zone” sign tells you that the special reduced school-zone speed limit is over. After passing this sign, you may resume driving at the regular posted speed for that roadway, if conditions are safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light you must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection,b:Maintain your normal speed and turn immediately,c:Stop and wait for a police officer's instruction
note: When turning right on a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or entering the intersection. A green light allows you to turn if it is safe, but it does not give you the right-of-way over pedestrians.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To indicate what a driver must or must not do,b:To warn of hazards ahead,c:To provide information about nearby services
note: Regulatory signs are used to tell drivers what they must do or must not do, such as obeying speed limits, lane use controls, parking restrictions, and turn prohibitions. They are legally enforceable and are different from warning signs (which alert you to hazards) and guide signs (which give directions or service information).

question: What does a painted arrow in a lane usually indicate?
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow,b:The arrow is decorative and may be ignored,c:Drivers should always stop before following the arrow
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the roadway show what movement is allowed or required from that lane, such as straight, left turn, right turn, or a combination. When you are in a lane with a single arrow, you must make the movement shown by the arrow when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Stop and treat it like a stop sign,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present,c:Continue because they have the right-of-way
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in or approaching the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe, just as you would at a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Signal in advance, slow gradually, move into the left lane when appropriate, and watch for oncoming vehicles/pedestrians,b:Speed up and turn quickly,c:Ignore rearview checks
note: To turn left safely, signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and move into the proper left lane or left-turn lane. Slow down smoothly, yield to oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians, and only turn when there is a safe gap. Sudden speeding or ignoring rear and side checks greatly increases crash risk.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to which of these?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A yield sign,c:The signal is broken
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a full stop, yield to pedestrians and any traffic with the right-of-way, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: \Highway hypnosis\" can result from:"
options: a:Getting extra sleep before a trip,b:Frequent rest stops,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning mirrors, instruments, and the road environment. Your mind drifts, reaction time slows, and you may experience brief micro‑sleeps. To prevent this, take regular breaks, keep your eyes moving, and stay mentally engaged with the driving task.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended upward indicates what maneuver?
options: a:The driver plans to turn left.,b:The driver plans to turn right.,c:The driver plans to stop.,d:The driver plans to accelerate.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn. A left arm bent upward at the elbow with the hand pointing up means a right turn. A left arm bent downward at the elbow with the hand pointing down means slowing or stopping. Knowing these signals helps you understand other drivers and communicate clearly if your signals fail.

question: What is the meaning of a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or entering the intersection.

question: Round traffic signs generally warn drivers of what ahead?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Railroad crossings.,d:Stop signs.
note: In the U.S., round traffic signs are used specifically for railroad crossings. A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters “RR” warns you that you are approaching a railroad crossing and should slow down, look, and listen for trains.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Turn on your windshield wipers,c:Turn on your headlights
note: When visibility is reduced by fog, heavy rain, snow, or darkness, your first response should be to reduce your speed. Slowing down gives you more time to see and react to hazards. You should also turn on your low‑beam headlights and use windshield wipers as needed, but the most immediate safety step is to adjust your speed to what you can safely see.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of you. What should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: When a pedestrian starts to cross in front of you, you must slow down and be ready to stop. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and never try to beat them through the crossing.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.,c:Drive slower than surrounding traffic.,d:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.
note: The safest strategy is to travel with the flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of collisions.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren on, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,b:Pull to the right and stop.,c:Slow down and remain in your lane.,d:Accelerate to clear the way faster.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren on, you must move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,d:You may pass at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They follow different traffic laws than cars.,c:They always have the right-of-way.,d:They travel faster than cars.
note: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in traffic or blind spots, so they are easier to overlook. Drivers must scan carefully and give them extra space.

question: In which conditions does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:When driving at night.,c:On wet or icy roads.,d:When driving on straight, level roads.
note: Stopping distance increases whenever traction is reduced or speed is higher. Wet, icy, or loose road surfaces greatly reduce tire grip, so it takes much longer to stop. In these conditions you should slow down and leave extra following distance.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:The person driving the car.,b:Passengers when they are on a long drive.,c:All occupants of a vehicle, on every trip.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts at all times; an unbelted passenger can become a projectile in a crash.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what is a reliable way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Take a cold shower to sober up.,d:Wait five minutes after your last drink and then drive carefully.
note: The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive. Plan ahead for a sober driver, taxi, rideshare, or public transit. Coffee, cold showers, or waiting a few minutes do not reduce your blood alcohol level or make you safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to let other drivers know you're turning.,d:Turn off your signal to avoid confusing others.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your wheels straight and your turn signal on. If you are hit from behind while your wheels are turned left, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight reduces this risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a multi-lane roadway, you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by adjusting speed or changing lanes if safe.,b:Honk at incoming traffic.,c:Always maintain your current speed regardless of others.
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane from an on‑ramp or side road. On a multi‑lane road, you should adjust your speed and, if it is safe, change lanes or create space so merging drivers can enter smoothly. Never rely on your horn or insist on keeping your exact speed if it prevents safe merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Coming to an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear,b:Slow and drive through if no cars are visible,c:Wait for a flashing green light
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should:
options: a:Split the difference and pass between them,b:Pull onto the shoulder immediately,c:Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist to avoid handling two hazards at once
note: When you face hazards on both sides, handle them one at a time. Allow the oncoming car to pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist only when you have enough space and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When your traffic signal is a green arrow,b:When entering a street from a garage or alley,c:When they are on a road to your right and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must stop if necessary and yield to all traffic and pedestrians already on the road or sidewalk. At an unmarked intersection, you yield to vehicles on your right when you arrive at the same time, not to those on your left.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:Beer impairs less than wine.,b:Wine impairs less than beer.,c:The type of beverage does not change impairment, amount consumed matters.,d:Hard ciders and mixed drinks impair more than straight spirits always.
note: Impairment depends on how much alcohol you consume and how quickly your body absorbs it, not on whether it is beer, wine, or liquor. A standard drink of each has about the same amount of alcohol and can cause similar impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When pulling forward from a driveway, what must you do regarding the sidewalk?
options: a:Have the right-of-way over pedestrians in the sidewalk area.,b:Must slow down before crossing the sidewalk area.,c:Must come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk area.
note: When exiting a driveway, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and other sidewalk users. Only proceed when the sidewalk and roadway are clear and it is safe.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This checks the blind spot that mirrors cannot show. Do not rely only on mirrors, and you do not need to honk your horn for normal lane changes.

question: What does an orange-colored roadway sign generally indicate?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for road work. They alert you to construction, maintenance, or work zones so you can slow down, be prepared for workers or equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

question: Guide signs that provide direction and mileage are usually which color?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Guide signs that show directions, route information, and distances are usually green with white lettering. They help you find exits, cities, and routes on highways and other major roads.

question: When you hear a siren behind you while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Slow down, then pull over to the right and stop when safe.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Continue driving normally.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely slow down, signal, and pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can create a clear path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, who must you slow for and yield to?
options: a:Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Do not enter until it is safe and clear.

question: Alcohol consumption causes:
options: a:Improved coordination,b:Impaired concentration, coordination, and slowed judgment,c:No effect on driving ability
note: Alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely by harming concentration, coordination, judgment, and vision. Even small amounts can slow your reactions and make it harder to stay in your lane, judge distances, and respond to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Signal only if visible traffic is present,b:Signal only at night,c:Always signal your intentions, even if no traffic is visible
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your actions and helps prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two‑lane road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,b:Maintain your slow speed until the traffic clears,c:Prevent other cars from passing you
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two‑lane road, you are impeding traffic. When it is safe, pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout so faster vehicles can pass.

question: Which are the most effective safety restraints in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash is using both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together. The seat belt keeps you properly positioned and restrained, while the airbag provides extra cushioning in a collision.

question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or OTC medicine?
options: a:The medicine will cancel out the alcohol.,b:The alcohol helps the medicine work better.,c:The combination can multiply impairing effects.,d:There is no interaction between alcohol and medicines.
note: Alcohol can interact with prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines and greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and slowed reactions. The combination can multiply the impairing effects and make driving especially dangerous.

question: Most of the information you need to drive safely comes primarily from which sense?
options: a:Seeing,b:Hearing,c:Touch
note: Nearly all the information you use while driving comes through your eyes. You must constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and behind using your mirrors so you can see hazards early and respond safely.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver,c:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly
note: Drivers must use care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when pedestrians are careless or not following the rules. You should slow down and be prepared to stop whenever a pedestrian is in or about to enter your path, whether or not they are in a crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line when:
options: a:When the car ahead is disabled,b:Doing so would interfere with traffic,c:Turning left into a driveway
note: A single broken line (white between lanes in the same direction, yellow between opposite directions) means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe. You must not cross if doing so would interfere with other traffic or create a hazard.

question: A driver ahead is distracted by passengers and driving with one hand. How should you respond?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Avoid following the driver's example.,c:Know that the driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.
note: When you see a driver who is distracted or not fully in control, increase your following distance and give them extra space. This gives you more time to react if they make a sudden or unsafe move.

question: Must traffic signs and pavement markings be obeyed?
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that all road users must obey. Following them helps keep traffic orderly and reduces crashes by making everyone’s actions more predictable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,d:Leave wheels in any position if parking brake is set.
note: When you park facing uphill next to a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Which statement about bicyclists is correct?
options: a:Bicyclists may ride two abreast on roadways when it does not impede traffic and local law does not prohibit it.,b:Bicyclists may ride two abreast on bike paths or lanes except where signs prohibit it.,c:Bicyclists always have right-of-way over pedestrians.,d:Bicyclists must always ride on the sidewalk.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers of vehicles and may ride two abreast on the roadway as long as they do not impede normal and reasonable traffic flow and local law does not prohibit it. They do not always have right‑of‑way over pedestrians and are not required to ride on sidewalks, which are often unsafe or illegal for bikes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Follow what surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger,c:Ignore the flagger because signs control traffic
note: In construction or work zones, you must obey the directions of flaggers. They are authorized to control traffic and may override traffic signals or signs to keep workers and drivers safe. Always follow the flagger’s hand signals or signs, even if they differ from other controls.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The reduced noise of large vehicles.,d:The ability to pass the truck at any time.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need more distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, avoid cutting in front of them, don’t brake suddenly, and give them extra space so they have enough room to stop safely.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding,b:Go through as soon as one train passes,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train
note: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, after one train passes, another train may be coming on a different track. Stay stopped until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other trains are approaching before you proceed.

question: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights and approaches, what should you do?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights and/or a siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and come to a complete stop, remaining stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. This gives them a clear path and reduces the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Night drives,c:Slow speeds
note: Higher speeds greatly increase both the distance needed to stop and the force of any impact. Because stopping distance grows with speed and crash energy increases with the square of speed, driving fast makes it much harder to avoid hazards and makes any collision more severe.

question: Which is a key practice for driving safely at night?
options: a:Not drive if you are tired.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Make sure your headlights are working properly.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to see hazards in time. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react and stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. You should also avoid driving when tired and ensure your headlights work properly, but increasing following distance is a key active driving practice every time you drive at night.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:It helps cars behind you move faster,b:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving,c:You will need extra space to open your door
note: When stopped on an uphill slope, the vehicle in front of you may roll backward slightly when the driver releases the brake to move forward. Leaving extra space in front of your vehicle helps prevent a rear‑end collision if the vehicle ahead rolls back before accelerating.

question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp properly?
options: a:Slow down before entering the ramp.,b:Begin to slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,c:Keep the same speed while on the ramp.,d:Stop on the ramp to check directions.
note: When exiting a freeway, stay at freeway speed until you are in the exit lane and on the ramp, then begin to slow down to the posted ramp speed. Braking before you enter the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive faster to cut through the water layer.,b:Spin the steering wheel quickly when water is felt.,c:Do not speed when the roads are wet and maintain good tire tread and pressure.,d:Deflate your tires slightly before heavy rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce this risk, slow down on wet roads and make sure your tires have good tread and are properly inflated. Driving faster, turning the wheel sharply, or changing tire pressure incorrectly will increase your chances of losing control.

question: When may you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Whenever you turn on your four-way flashers.,b:If no part of the vehicle is on the roadway.,c:To consult a map or ask directions.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: On freeways, the shoulder is for emergencies only, such as breakdowns or medical problems. You may not stop there just to read a map, use your phone, or rest. If you must use the shoulder in an emergency, pull as far off the roadway as possible and turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers can see you.

question: What can happen when alcohol and drugs are consumed together?
options: a:Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:Help cure your illness.,d:Have no effect on your driving ability.
note: Mixing alcohol with any drug—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. This makes driving far more dangerous and increases your risk of a crash.

question: How must a driver treat pedestrians in the roadway?
options: a:Only yield when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:Yield only if a traffic light is present.,c:Make sure the pedestrian notices your vehicle before proceeding.,d:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if they are not legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers must always do everything possible to avoid hitting pedestrians. Even if a pedestrian is crossing illegally or outside a crosswalk, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield if needed to prevent a collision. You can never insist on your right‑of‑way if it would put a pedestrian in danger.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Most general warning signs are diamond‑shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: If an emergency vehicle is behind you but is not using its lights or siren, it is operating as a regular vehicle. You are not required to pull over or clear the lane; instead, continue driving safely and normally, obeying all traffic laws and speed limits.

question: Which statement about pavement lines is true?
options: a:Red lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.,b:White lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.,c:Yellow lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.,d:White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.
note: In the U.S., white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on multi‑lane roads and highways. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross broken white lines when it is safe and legal to change lanes.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels frequently.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Snow tires can improve traction on slippery roads.
note: Cruise control should not be used on snow, ice, or in other slippery winter conditions because it can cause you to lose control if the vehicle starts to skid. In winter, you should drive with extra caution, check fluids like antifreeze and washer fluid often, and consider snow tires to improve traction.

question: When towing a trailer, which equipment should it definitely have?
options: a:Tires that are properly inflated.,b:Properly mounted and lubricated wheels covered with fenders or mud guards.,c:The proper lamps and reflectors.,d:All of the above.
note: When towing a trailer, it must have all required safety equipment: properly inflated tires, properly mounted and lubricated wheels with fenders or mud guards to control spray and debris, and the correct lamps and reflectors so other drivers can see your trailer and understand your movements. All of these are essential for safe towing.

question: You should always signal when you are:
options: a:Changing lanes,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area,d:All of the above
note: You should always use your turn signal any time you intend to change where your vehicle is going in relation to other traffic. This includes changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from an alley, driveway, or parking area. Signaling gives other road users time to react safely to your movements.

question: When towing a loaded trailer that weighs more than half the towing vehicle or 3,000+ pounds, the trailer must have:
options: a:Brakes and breakaway protection,b:Only hub caps,c:No special equipment
note: Trailers over specified weights must be equipped with brakes and breakaway protection for safety and legal compliance.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, what should you remember?
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop, especially at highway speeds or when loaded. You should leave extra space in front of trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, and expect that they cannot stop as quickly as smaller vehicles.

question: How should you approach crossing railroad tracks safely?
options: a:Listen, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe,b:Look only when lights are flashing,c:Cross quickly when you hear a train in the distance
note: At railroad crossings, slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and all signals and gates indicate it is safe. Never try to beat a train or cross when warning devices are active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror only.,c:Over your left shoulder.,d:At the road ahead only.
note: Before changing lanes to the left, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your left shoulder to see the area your mirrors do not show, called the blind spot. This helps you make sure there is no vehicle or motorcycle hidden beside you before you move over.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:
options: a:Often have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle,b:Make no driving errors,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. This increases the chance of drifting out of your lane, missing hazards, and reacting too slowly to traffic changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning required?
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
note: You are legally required to signal before turning or changing lanes so others have time to react. Signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the turn in most areas, and more at higher speeds—then keep signaling through the turn.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Limit your driving to weekdays.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash. It keeps you from being thrown from the vehicle and helps you stay in control during emergency maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic?
options: a:Should leave room on your right for other vehicles to pass.,b:Must yield to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Must not cross any solid yellow line.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard. Wait for a safe gap in traffic, then turn, keeping your wheels straight until you actually begin the turn so you are not pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver cuts you off?
options: a:Call the police immediately.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm, slow down if needed, and create space so they can move away from you. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or any actions that could escalate the situation, and focus on keeping a safe following distance.

question: When driving at night and another vehicle is approaching, your headlights should be set to:
options: a:High beam,b:Low beam,c:Parking lights only
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, use low-beam headlights so you do not blind the other driver. High beams should only be used when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not following another vehicle closely.

question: When you first turn the ignition on before starting the engine, instrument panel warning lamps should:
options: a:Never illuminate unless there's a malfunction,b:Illuminate briefly to show they are functioning,c:Remain off until the engine is running
note: Instrument panel warning lights normally come on briefly when you turn the key to the ON position before starting the engine. This is a self‑check so you can see that the bulbs and systems are working. A light that never comes on at all may indicate a burned‑out bulb or electrical problem.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection,b:Stop but you may proceed if clear,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears
note: A red arrow means the movement in the direction of the arrow is not allowed. You must stop and remain stopped at the stop line or crosswalk and may not turn or proceed in that direction until a green light or green arrow appears and it is safe to go.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving is the practice of constantly scanning for hazards, anticipating what other road users might do, and adjusting your speed and position early to avoid conflicts and crashes. It focuses on staying safe rather than reacting aggressively to other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Back up slowly.
note: When a signal turns green, you do not have an absolute right‑of‑way. First, check the intersection and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still clearing the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe, even though the light is green.

question: A good general rule regarding passing is:
options: a:Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Constantly try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic
note: Passing always carries extra risk because it puts you in or near oncoming traffic and in other drivers’ blind spots. A safe general rule is to travel with the flow of traffic and pass only when it is clearly necessary, legal, and you have enough space and visibility to complete the maneuver safely.

question: Why is driving at night more difficult than in daylight?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night,c:It is more likely to rain at night
note: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as far or as clearly as in daylight. Headlights limit your field of vision, making it harder to spot hazards, judge distances, and see pedestrians or animals. You should slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a multi-lane road signals:
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction where lane changes and passing are permitted,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is forbidden,c:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is forbidden
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes and pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors, blind spots, and signaling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving behind a slow vehicle on a four-lane highway, before changing lanes you must:
options: a:Make sure there is sufficient room in traffic, check blind spots, and signal at least 100 feet before moving,b:Only signal if someone is behind you,c:Change lanes immediately without signaling
note: Before changing lanes to pass a slower vehicle on a multi-lane highway, you must make sure there is enough space in the lane you want to enter, check your mirrors and blind spots, and signal in advance. Signaling and checking blind spots help prevent collisions with vehicles you may not see in your mirrors.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and be prepared to stop if necessary,b:Always come to a full stop, even when clear,c:Only slow down for emergency vehicles
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Stop if needed to avoid interfering with other road users.

question: When stopped in traffic at a railroad crossing without gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.,c:There is enough room ahead for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks before you drive onto them.,d:You may stop on the tracks if necessary for traffic.
note: At a railroad crossing, you must never enter the tracks unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks completely. Do not stop on the tracks and do not pass other vehicles when approaching or crossing; trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to continue carefully through an intersection on a yellow light?
options: a:If there are pedestrians crossing,b:If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane,c:If you are already in the intersection or cannot safely stop before entering
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection or are so close that stopping safely is not possible, continue through carefully. Always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens on.

question: Which signal tells you to slow and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, being prepared to stop if needed. It does not require a full stop unless necessary to avoid a hazard. A flashing red light means stop completely, then proceed when it is safe, like a stop sign. A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red and you should stop if you can do so safely.

question: When it begins to rain and visibility is reduced, you should:
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed to keep traffic moving,c:Pull into the passing lane and stay there
note: When it starts to rain, roads become especially slippery and visibility often decreases. You should reduce your speed and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes very poor, move to a safe location off the roadway and wait for conditions to improve. Driving at the maximum speed or staying in the passing lane in poor conditions is unsafe.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow and a red light together, what does that mean?
options: a:You may only drive straight ahead.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You must wait for the solid green light to go in any direction.,d:You may turn in any direction with caution.
note: A green arrow with a red circular light means you may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow, and only if the intersection is clear and it is safe to go. The red circular light still applies to all other movements, so you must stop for any direction not indicated by the arrow.

question: What information do highway pavement markings provide?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Highway pavement markings provide important information about lane use, traffic flow direction, passing zones, turn lanes, and where stopping or crossing is allowed. These markings must be obeyed just like signs and signals, because they help organize traffic and improve safety.

question: What can happen when alcohol and another drug are combined?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased,b:No effect will occur,c:The combination will always reduce the effects of each
note: Alcohol combined with many drugs, including some prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. Because of this unpredictable and often stronger combined effect, you should never mix alcohol with other drugs when you plan to drive.

question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:
options: a:Stop at or near the scene, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles,b:Leave immediately to avoid liability,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct cars around the wreck
note: After a collision, you are legally required to stop at or near the scene. Protect yourself and others by staying out of traffic lanes, turning off the ignitions of damaged vehicles to reduce fire risk, and calling for help. Do not leave the scene or stand where you could be struck by passing traffic.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop,b:Always sound your horn when you see children,c:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully on both sides of the street, and be ready to stop whenever children are in or near the crosswalk. Use extra caution during school hours and when crossing guards are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, it's important to:
options: a:Signal ahead, check blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before entering,b:Only signal if other drivers are present,c:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance so others know your intentions, check your mirrors, and quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and you can change lanes smoothly and safely.

question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection,b:Speed up to clear the intersection,c:Continue as you have the right-of-way
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: Which of these are used on some highways to direct drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:Flashing yellow lights.,c:White lines on the road shoulders.,d:Arrow markings or lane arrows.
note: Arrow markings painted on the pavement or shown on overhead signs tell you which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. You must be in a lane with the correct arrow for the movement you intend to make.

question: If you are charged with DUI and refuse the required chemical test, what is a likely consequence?
options: a:You will only lose your license for refusing if also convicted of another traffic offense.,b:You will only lose your license if convicted of DUI.,c:Refusing the test has no administrative consequences.,d:You may lose your driver license for a minimum of 12 months because you refused the test.
note: Under implied consent laws, driving in Hawaii means you agree to take a chemical test if lawfully requested. If you refuse, your license can be revoked administratively for at least one year, even if you are not convicted of DUI.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go,b:Turn your wheel into oncoming traffic,c:Overcorrect sharply
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Avoid slamming on the brakes or jerking the wheel, because sudden movements can make the skid worse.

question: If you must make a quick stop and your vehicle does not have ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal continuously.,b:Firmly pump the brake pedal.,c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,d:Shift into neutral and coast to a stop.
note: In a quick stop without ABS, use firm, repeated pumping of the brake pedal. This helps you slow or stop quickly while still allowing you to steer and reducing the chance of locking the wheels and skidding.

question: When children ride in vehicles, they should:
options: a:Be properly secured in appropriate child seats or safety belts,b:Be safely held by a strong adult,c:Stand on the floor in the back seat
note: Children must always be secured in a child safety seat, booster, or seat belt that fits their age, size, and weight. Holding a child or letting them stand in the vehicle is extremely dangerous because, in a crash, no one can hold a child against the forces involved.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning,b:It increases tire wear,c:It reduces fuel efficiency only
note: A leaky exhaust can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless gas, enter the passenger area. Breathing carbon monoxide can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any exhaust leak should be repaired immediately to protect everyone in the vehicle.

question: What is the proper lighting to use when driving in fog?
options: a:Hazard lights,b:Low beam headlights,c:High beams
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. The light from high beams reflects off the water droplets in the fog and shines back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as possible and stop,b:Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane,c:Speed up to get out of the way quickly
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by moving as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Do not block intersections, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. Never speed up or try to outrun it.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that which light will soon appear?
options: a:Flashing yellow,b:Steady green,c:Steady red
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, proceed with caution through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Sharply away from the curb,b:Slightly to the right,c:Sharply toward the curb
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward the curb and the car will be stopped by the curb instead of rolling into traffic. When parking uphill or downhill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

question: If you must drive in foggy conditions, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Hazard lights only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Parking lights or hazard lights alone do not provide enough forward illumination and can confuse other drivers.

question: If you change the address on your vehicle registration, you must:
options: a:Notify the appropriate motor vehicle/registration authority within the required time (often 30 days),b:Notify the County Department of Finance only when selling the car,c:Wait until your next renewal to update it
note: When you move, you must update the address on your vehicle registration within a set time period (commonly 30 days) with the appropriate motor vehicle or finance/registration authority. This ensures renewal notices, tax bills, and other legal notices reach you at your correct address.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped in line at a stop sign and the vehicles ahead have cleared the intersection. If there is no cross traffic, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Come to a complete stop at the stop sign or line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign if the road looks clear.,d:Honk to warn cross traffic before going.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if the car ahead of you already stopped and went. After stopping, you must yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way before proceeding.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It improves driving skills but impairs judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.,d:It sharpens perception in small amounts.
note: Alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely by slowing reaction time, blurring vision, affecting coordination, and impairing judgment. Even small amounts can make it harder to judge speed, distance, and traffic situations, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: For a road test, the vehicle you provide must be:
options: a:In safe operating condition with required inspection and insurance,b:Owned by the testing agency,c:Allowed to have safety defects for the test
note: For a road test, you must provide a vehicle that is in safe working order, free of obvious defects, and properly registered and insured. Required safety equipment (lights, brakes, signals, tires, etc.) must function correctly, and any required inspection must be current.

question: On a road without sidewalks a pedestrian should walk on which side?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic,b:The side on which traffic is moving (same side),c:The side facing oncoming traffic
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and move out of the way if needed, improving their safety.

question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow for turn lanes?
options: a:Prepare to stop — a red arrow is coming unless you are already in the intersection,b:Merge immediately into the lane indicated by the arrow,c:Proceed without changing speed or position
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending and a red arrow will appear soon. You should stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it appears, continue and clear the intersection; do not stop in the intersection.

question: When passing a large truck, what should the driver of a small vehicle expect?
options: a:Gusts of wind from the large vehicle that may affect steering,b:Loud music from the truck's cabin,c:Extra pollution with no handling effects
note: When passing a large truck, expect strong wind gusts and air turbulence that can push or pull your vehicle sideways. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be prepared to adjust your steering to stay in your lane.

question: About how quickly does the average body process alcohol?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:One alcoholic drink per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.,d:Alcohol is processed instantly.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at about one standard drink per hour. This rate does not speed up with coffee, cold showers, or exercise, and can vary with body size, sex, health, and food intake.

question: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop in the location under which condition?
options: a:To avoid conflict with other traffic,b:To unload packages for an extended time,c:To stop for any reason briefly
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may not stop your vehicle at the curb or roadside except to obey a traffic control device or to avoid a conflict with other traffic. You may not stop there to load, unload, or wait, even briefly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection, you must stop when you see which of these signals?
options: a:A flashing red light,b:A steady yellow light,c:A yellow arrow
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. A steady yellow or yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to change to red, but does not itself always require a full stop if you can safely clear the intersection.

question: To practice defensive driving, you should:
options: a:Scan ahead for developing traffic situations, maintain proper following distance, and have alternate plans,b:Focus only on the car directly in front of you,c:Drive as slowly as possible at all times
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead and around you, keeping a safe following distance so you have time to react, and always having an alternate plan if something unexpected happens. Focusing only on the car in front or driving extremely slowly can actually create hazards instead of preventing them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a required action when changing lanes?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check your blind spot.,c:Begin signaling after you start the lane change.,d:Ignore blind spots if mirrors look clear.
note: When changing lanes, you must signal in advance—at least 100 feet before changing lanes in lower‑speed areas—and also check your blind spots by quickly looking over your shoulder. Mirrors alone do not show everything next to your vehicle, so a shoulder check plus proper signaling time helps other drivers anticipate your move and prevents collisions.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to clear the crossing faster.,c:Ignore warning signs if you do not see a train.
note: As you approach a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is approaching, you must stop at the required distance from the tracks and proceed only when the tracks are clear and signals indicate it is safe.

question: What should you never allow when towing a trailer?
