options: a:Have someone ride in the trailer to keep the load steady.,b:Allow only adults to ride in the trailer.,c:Never allow anyone to ride in the trailer.
note: No one should ride in a trailer being towed. Trailers are not designed to protect passengers in sudden stops, swerves, or crashes, and many states specifically prohibit people from riding in them. All passengers should ride in the towing vehicle with proper seats and restraints.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous and to be approached with caution,b:Generally safe to cross without stopping,c:Good places to park your car
note: Railroad crossings are high‑risk areas because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way. You should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if signals, gates, or your own observations indicate a train is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use your headlights.,b:Use hand signals.,c:Sound your horn.,d:Use your hazard lights instead.
note: If your turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show when you intend to turn or change lanes. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, up for a right turn, and down for slowing or stopping so other drivers clearly understand your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a turn, what should you do?
options: a:Use your signal several seconds before the turn,b:Turn the wheel immediately,c:Increase your speed
note: Before turning, signal well in advance—typically at least the last 100 feet in city driving or about three to four seconds before the turn. This gives other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians time to react to your intended movement.

question: If you're in an accident and someone is injured, you should:
options: a:Not move the injured unless necessary, keep them warm and provide first aid,b:Immediately move them away from the scene,c:Always leave the injured where they are without giving help
note: After a crash with injuries, call emergency services and do not move injured people unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Keep them warm, reassure them, and provide basic first aid within your ability until professional help arrives.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A yield sign,c:A slow sign
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Can prescription and over-the-counter medicines affect your driving?
options: a:No — only illegal drugs impair driving,b:Only medicines taken with alcohol have effects,c:Yes — many medicines can impair driving ability
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reaction time. Always read labels and ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine may affect your driving before you drive after taking it.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply decline drinks when offered while at the event.,c:Call a taxi only after you feel intoxicated.,d:Drink lots of water while drinking alcohol.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide before you drink that you will not drive and to arrange a sober driver or alternate transportation. Once you have been drinking, your judgment is impaired and you may wrongly think you are still safe to drive.

question: Which practice is safest when negotiating a curve?
options: a:Slow down on entry and gradually speed up on exit,b:Maintain the same speed from start to finish,c:Speed up entering and slow down when exiting
note: Before a curve, slow down to a safe speed while your vehicle is still straight, then steer smoothly through the curve and gradually accelerate as you exit. Entering too fast or braking hard in the curve can cause loss of traction and control.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A deaf person.,b:A person involved with a traffic study.,c:A blind person.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. You must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop well before the crosswalk, and never honk or rev your engine, as this can confuse or frighten the person or the guide dog.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the wheel straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas, then brake gently when under control,b:Brake hard immediately,c:Maintain speed and steer straight to the shoulder
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and slowly ease your foot off the accelerator. Do not brake hard. When the vehicle has slowed and you have control, steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently to stop.

question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren?
options: a:Only if it is behind you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of which direction it is coming from, pull to the right and stop.,d:Only when you are in an intersection.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling as far to the right as possible and stopping, regardless of whether they are behind you, approaching from ahead, or coming from a side street. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The middle of the intersection.,b:The right lane.,c:The left lane.,d:From the shoulder of the road.
note: On a one‑way street, a left turn should begin from the leftmost lane that is lawfully available. When turning left from a multilane one‑way street onto another one‑way street, you normally start from the left lane and turn into a legal lane on the new street, unless signs or lane markings direct you otherwise.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,d:All of the above.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad gates. You must stop when a flagger or signal tells you to, and you must also remember that many crossings have only signs or pavement markings with no flashing lights or gates. Because all three statements are correct, “All of the above” is the true statement.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:To stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:To run out in front of you without looking.
note: Children often act unpredictably and may run into the street without looking or understanding traffic dangers. When driving where children are present—near schools, parks, or neighborhoods—slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your car, you should:
options: a:Maintain a steady speed and, if needed, slightly adjust speed to allow a safe pass while staying in your lane.,b:Pull off the road immediately whenever someone tries to pass you.,c:Signal to the other driver when you think it is safe for them to pass.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce speed to help them pass safely. Continuously scan for oncoming traffic so you are aware of developing hazards, but you are not responsible for judging or signaling when it is safe for them to pass. Never speed up while being passed, and do not pull off the road unless necessary for safety.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians have no right-of-way.,d:Only yield if the pedestrian is in the center of the road.
note: At any marked or unmarked crosswalk, drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are in the crosswalk. Slow or stop as needed so pedestrians can cross safely before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady green light, what should you do?
options: a:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe, but you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection, and be ready to stop if the light changes.

question: When driving in bad weather, what spacing adjustment should you make?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather.,d:Tailgate to prevent merging vehicles from cutting in.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or other poor conditions, increase your following distance so you have more time and space to see hazards, react, and stop without skidding.

question: When do roads become especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:The day following rainfall.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,d:Only when the temperature is below freezing.
note: During the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm, water mixes with oil and other residue on the road surface, making it especially slippery. Slow down and increase following distance during this time.

question: A single broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is allowed when safe,b:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is allowed,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is prohibited
note: A single broken (dashed) yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing when it can be done safely and is not otherwise prohibited by signs or conditions.

question: Which factors influence how alcohol affects a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach.,b:Body weight of the individual.,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects people differently based on several factors, including body weight, how much and how quickly you drink, and whether you have food in your stomach. Food slows the absorption of alcohol into the bloodstream but does not prevent impairment. More time between drinks also allows your body to process some alcohol, affecting your blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road,b:Toward the right side of the road,c:Directly at the headlights
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare while still seeing the road, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge line or right side of the roadway as a guide until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a speed limit sign posted on an exit ramp?
options: a:Never drive slower than that posted speed on the ramp,b:After you are in the exit lane, slow smoothly to at or below the posted ramp speed,c:Regard the posted limit as merely a suggestion
note: The speed shown on an exit ramp sign is the maximum safe speed for ideal conditions on that ramp, not a minimum. You should move into the exit lane first, then slow smoothly to at or below the posted ramp speed before entering the curve. Always adjust lower for traffic, weather, or road conditions.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, even if they are crossing against the signal. Stop and allow them to cross safely, and proceed only when the crosswalk is clear.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It helps you see side traffic more clearly.,d:It does not affect vision.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows. You see less to the sides and are more focused straight ahead, which makes it easier to miss hazards coming from the sides. This is one reason higher speeds require greater caution and longer following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before starting your turn.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you through.,d:Begin the turn into the first lane and then shift.
note: When turning left, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards. If large vehicles or heavy traffic block your view, wait behind the crosswalk and keep your wheels straight until you have a clear line of sight and can complete the entire turn safely.

question: How should drivers react to a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Increase their speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, not stop. You should slow down, scan carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe. Be prepared to yield if necessary, but a complete stop is not required unless other conditions make it unsafe to proceed.

question: It is important to slow down in which situations?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections/railroad crossings, and when roads are wet or slippery,b:Only on freeways,c:Only in parking lots
note: You should reduce speed whenever conditions make normal speeds unsafe. This includes narrow or winding roads, intersections and railroad crossings, hills and curves, areas with pedestrians or limited visibility, and any time the road is wet, icy, or otherwise slippery. Slowing down gives you more time and space to react and helps prevent skids.

question: The most important speed-management rule for curves is to:
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Drive the posted speed limit on entry and slow later,c:Accelerate gently before entering the curve
note: Before entering a curve, slow to a safe speed while your tires are still straight. Once in the curve, sudden braking or sharp steering can cause you to lose traction because of inertia and centrifugal force. Entering too fast is a common cause of crashes on curves, so adjust your speed in advance and then maintain a steady speed through the turn.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Increase speed to power through standing water,b:Reduce your speed when roads are wet,c:Drive through deeper water to clear the tires
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, which is more likely at higher speeds on wet pavement. To reduce the risk, slow down when roads are wet, avoid sudden steering or braking, and drive in the tracks of vehicles ahead when possible. Proper tire tread and inflation also help prevent hydroplaning.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct action?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Speed up and steer back on quickly.,c:Slow down, stay parallel to the road, and gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,d:Immediately pull all the way off the road.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, keep calm and avoid jerking the wheel. Ease off the accelerator, keep the car straight and parallel to the roadway, slow down gradually, and when the car is under control and traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: The habit of turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes or merging is:
options: a:A good driving habit,b:Unnecessary,c:A bad driving habit
note: Before changing lanes or merging, always check mirrors and then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving. This head check covers the blind spot that mirrors cannot show and is an essential safe‑driving habit.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line,b:Passing is permitted from either lane,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe. Traffic on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: Who is responsible for the mechanical condition of a vehicle you are driving?
options: a:The legal owner of the vehicle.,b:The garage mechanic.,c:The driver operating the vehicle.,d:The vehicle manufacturer.
note: The driver is responsible for making sure the vehicle being driven is in safe operating condition, even if they do not own it. You must not drive a vehicle you know, or should know, is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The recommended speed for bad weather.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:The exact speed that guarantees you won't get a ticket.,d:A minimum safe speed.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed for that road in ideal conditions. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or other hazards, you must slow down below the posted limit to a speed that is safe for conditions.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, the best action is to:
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help,b:Get out and walk for help immediately,c:Lie down in the car and sleep
note: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay in your vehicle. The car provides shelter from wind and cold, makes you easier for rescuers to find, and reduces the risk of getting lost or disoriented in low visibility. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup, and use lights or signals so others can see you.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) signs usually indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Pedestrian crossings.,c:School zones or school crossing areas.,d:Speed limits.
note: Pentagonal (five‑sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway, especially during school hours.

question: What is the best way to deal with a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: When another driver is following too closely (tailgating), the safest response is to create space and let them pass. If possible, change lanes safely or gradually slow down so they can go around you. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as these actions can increase the risk of a rear‑end collision or road rage.

question: Which behavior best describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring at objects off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation.,c:Only watching the vehicle directly ahead.,d:Checking mirrors regularly and scanning the road.
note: An inattentive driver is someone whose mind or eyes are not focused on the driving task. Staring at objects off the roadway or daydreaming means you are not actively scanning traffic, signs, and road conditions, which greatly increases the chance of missing hazards. Safe drivers keep their attention on the road and regularly scan mirrors and the surrounding area.

question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what is the correct response?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,d:Back up carefully to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you must never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the highway or on the exit ramp. Continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route that allows you to return to the exit you missed. This prevents sudden, unexpected maneuvers that can cause serious crashes at high speeds.

question: What must you have to drive a heavy truck in Hawaii?
options: a:Be at least 21 years old.,b:Have a valid driver license for the category of vehicle you wish to drive.,c:Have no special qualifications.
note: To drive a heavy or commercial truck, you must have a valid license for that specific class of vehicle (often a commercial driver license). The license class must match the size and type of vehicle you are driving.

question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, what should you generally do?
options: a:Enter slowly to avoid disrupting traffic.,b:Stop before merging to wait for a large gap.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge when safe.,d:Turn on your hazard lights until fully merged.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the highway, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary.

question: If you approach an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived,b:Stop to watch and take pictures,c:Always stop even if it causes a traffic backup
note: If you come upon a crash, you must stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist. Otherwise, continue driving carefully, watching for people in the road and other hazards, so you do not create more danger or congestion.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce your speed, and pull to a safe area to stop,b:Turn off the ignition immediately,c:Open your hood and inspect the engine while driving slowly
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer but it will take much more effort. Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and carefully move to a safe place off the road to stop. Do not turn off the ignition while moving, as this can lock the steering.

question: If you're in a hurry and must back into the street, you should first:
options: a:Check around the car for children and objects before backing,b:Honk loudly before reversing,c:Rev the engine to warn animals
note: Before backing, always walk around the vehicle and check for children, animals, and objects. Backing has limited visibility, so checking behind and around the car first helps prevent collisions and injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, which blind-spot check should you make?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder, then signal.,b:Look over your right shoulder, then signal.,c:Look over both shoulders, then signal.,d:Check only your mirrors, no shoulder check required.
note: When changing lanes to the right, a vehicle can be hidden in the right-side blind spot where your mirrors do not show it. After checking your mirrors, you must quickly look over your right shoulder to check that blind spot, then signal and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,b:Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.,c:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point that drivers may appear intoxicated; simple measures like coffee or opening a window are insufficient to make a drowsy driver safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in rural areas.,b:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,c:When traveling in heavy construction zones.,d:Never illegal to drive below the limit.
note: Driving significantly below the speed of surrounding traffic, without a good reason like congestion or bad weather, can be unsafe and illegal because it disrupts the normal flow of traffic. You should generally travel at a speed that matches safe traffic flow, up to the posted limit.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Stop and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.,d:Pull over on the shoulder and reverse to the exit.
note: On a freeway, you must never back up on the travel lanes or shoulder, and you must not make a U-turn across the median. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway there, and then find a safe route back.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:Allow the motorcyclist the right half of a traffic lane.,b:Allow the motorcyclist the entire width of a traffic lane.,c:Begin moving past the motorcycle before your vehicle is entirely in the passing lane.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like a car. When passing, move fully into the adjacent lane, give the motorcycle plenty of space, and do not crowd or share the lane with the rider.

question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
options: a:If you cannot move right, wait until clear and then slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass,b:Move quickly to the left lane to stop them,c:Brake sharply to warn them
note: If someone is following too closely, create space and give them a safe chance to pass. If you cannot move to the right, wait for a clear stretch of road and gradually reduce your speed so they can go around you. Never slam on your brakes or make sudden moves, as this can cause a rear-end collision.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to those of smaller vehicles?
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks and buses have bigger blind spots than smaller vehicles. These blind spots are directly behind, directly in front, and along both sides, especially the right side. Avoid driving in these areas so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:Either driver may go first if they signal.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,d:The driver that indicates first by hand signals has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always make eye contact when possible and proceed only when it is clear who is going and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving on a multilane highway and wish to change lanes, you must signal at least:
options: a:100 feet before the lane change,b:50 feet before the lane change,c:Immediately before changing lanes
note: Before changing lanes, signal early enough to give other drivers time to see and react—at least 100 feet in most areas, and more at higher speeds such as on highways. After signaling, check mirrors and blind spots and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass a truck or bus regardless of conditions.,b:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate them.,c:Flash your lights to alert the driver.,d:Drive directly behind the truck to stay visible.
note: To stay out of a truck or bus driver’s blind spots, avoid driving right alongside the vehicle and do not follow closely behind it. If you cannot see the driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you. Pass promptly and safely, and leave extra space when merging in front.

question: On slick roads, how should you negotiate turns and curves?
options: a:Accelerate before turning to maintain momentum.,b:Use cruise control to maintain stability.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.,d:Change lanes quickly to avoid curves.
note: On slick or slippery roads, you have much less traction. Enter turns and curves more slowly than usual and avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration. Reducing speed before the curve helps you keep control and reduces the risk of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:Drivers should make hand motions to communicate who goes first.,d:The larger vehicle must yield to the smaller one.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps decide who goes first and prevents confusion and collisions.

question: Bicyclists are required to:
options: a:Always ride on sidewalks in business districts,b:Obey traffic laws, signs, and signals,c:Ride in the center of traffic lanes regardless of conditions
note: Bicycles are vehicles under the law and must follow traffic signs, signals, and regulations like other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best general practice?
options: a:Enter slowly and wait for an opening.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp, then merge.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.,d:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of freeway traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. Stopping on the ramp is dangerous because freeway drivers do not expect stopped vehicles.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:Because they are likely to be deaf,b:Because they are a traffic officer,c:Because they are blind
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. You must use extra caution: slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop so they can cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed.,b:Wait for the green light.,c:Proceed as directed by the officer.
note: You must follow the lawful instructions of a police officer, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs. If an officer directs you to proceed through a red light, you should carefully follow that direction, watching for other traffic and pedestrians as you go.

question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate:
options: a:No passing allowed from either direction,b:Passing is allowed for both directions,c:Passing is allowed at hilltops only
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal to do so, but not to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that indicate?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic on each side is moving in opposite directions, so you are on a two‑way road. The broken line also indicates that passing is allowed in either direction when it can be done safely and is not otherwise prohibited.

question: What happens to your tires on a wet road as your speed increases?
options: a:They become less effective at clearing water.,b:Good tires eliminate any danger from water.,c:Deep water is always safer than shallow water.,d:Speed has no effect on traction.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and can lead to hydroplaning, where the tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road, making steering and braking difficult or impossible.

question: Worn or bald tires can:
options: a:Increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and raise hydroplaning risk,b:Make turning easier,c:Reduce the chance of hydroplaning
note: Tires with worn or bald tread cannot grip the road well. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to control the vehicle in turns, and greatly raises the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads because the tread cannot channel water away effectively.

question: What type of sign warns drivers about potential hazards ahead?
options: a:Information signs,b:Warning signs,c:Regulatory signs
note: Warning signs are typically yellow with black symbols or words and are used to alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. Recognizing and responding to these signs early helps you adjust speed and position to avoid collisions.

question: If stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Lower your window and get out before the officer arrives,b:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer to approach, preparing paperwork when asked,c:Unbuckle and step out immediately
note: If stopped by law enforcement, you should pull over safely, stay in the vehicle unless directed otherwise, keep your hands visible—usually on the steering wheel—and have passengers keep their hands visible as well. Wait calmly for the officer to approach and only retrieve your license, registration, and insurance when the officer asks for them. This helps ensure everyone’s safety and reduces misunderstandings.

question: If two vehicles are side by side ahead of you and you are in a hurry, what should you do?
options: a:Tailgate the vehicle in the left lane and flash headlights.,b:Drive directly behind the right-lane vehicle to push it.,c:Maintain at least a two-second following interval in whichever lane you choose.,d:Swerve between lanes to advance.
note: When traffic ahead is side by side and you are in a hurry, you must still maintain a safe following distance—at least a two‑second gap in good conditions, and more in poor weather or at higher speeds. Tailgating, flashing headlights, or weaving between lanes increases crash risk and can be considered aggressive or reckless driving. Patience and proper following distance give you time to react to sudden stops or lane changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Has the right-of-way.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, then merge when it is safe. Vehicles already on the interstate have the right‑of‑way, so you must yield to them and adjust your speed or wait for a safe gap rather than forcing your way in.

question: When is it lawful to drink alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:If you are not the driver.,b:When riding in the back seat.,c:If you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.,d:It is illegal in most states to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road, regardless of whether you are the driver or a passenger.
note: In most U.S. jurisdictions, open‑container laws make it illegal to drink or possess an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road, whether you are the driver or a passenger. The safest rule is that no one in the vehicle should have an open alcoholic drink in any area normally occupied by the driver or passengers while on public streets or highways. Open containers, if allowed at all, must be stored in areas not normally occupied by people, such as a trunk.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and any vehicles that may not yield, and be prepared to stop if needed.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed gradually, keep wheels off pavement until safe, then steer gently back on,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force back onto pavement,c:Slam on brakes immediately
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while keeping your wheels on the shoulder. Once your speed is reduced and the way is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement to avoid skidding or losing control.

question: Where should you keep a copy of your vehicle inspection certificate?
options: a:Should be filed with your income tax return.,b:Should be kept in a safe place in your home.,c:Should be kept in the vehicle.
note: In many states, proof of inspection is recorded electronically or shown by a windshield sticker or registration document, not by keeping a loose inspection certificate in the vehicle. Important vehicle documents that are not legally required to be in the car are best stored securely at home to prevent loss, theft, or misuse.

question: When a traffic signal displays a green arrow for a turn, what does it mean?
options: a:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the arrow even if the circular light is red.,c:You may go straight regardless of the arrow.,d:The arrow only applies to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may turn in that direction even if the circular signal is red, but only in the direction the arrow points. Still check for pedestrians and any vehicles that may be in the intersection.

question: What practice can help you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk to alert other drivers.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to push them along.
note: To avoid sudden emergency stops, look well ahead in traffic and maintain a safe following distance. This gives you time to see brake lights, slowdowns, or hazards early so you can ease off the gas or brake smoothly instead of stopping abruptly.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition in your car?
options: a:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and see that all passengers do likewise.
note: Before starting the car, you should always buckle your own seat belt and make sure every passenger, adults and children, is properly buckled or in an appropriate child restraint. Making this a routine step before turning the ignition greatly improves safety for everyone in the vehicle.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train.,c:Look for a train, then speed up if none are visible.
note: Flashing railroad crossing signals mean a train is approaching. You must come to a complete stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and it is clearly safe to proceed. Never try to beat a train or speed up to cross while the signals are active.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) typically painted?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:Across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,d:At bus stops only.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and at pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop so they do not enter the crosswalk or intersection while waiting for a signal or sign.

question: If you change your address, when and how must you notify the county examiner of drivers?
options: a:By phone within 30 days.,b:In writing within 30 days.,c:In person within 10 days.,d:In writing within 10 days.
note: Many states require you to notify the licensing authority in writing within a set time after changing your address. Providing your new address, name, and license number within 30 days keeps your driving record and license information accurate and ensures you receive important notices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At intersections.,b:On hills and curves.,c:At railroad crossings.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is not allowed at intersections, on hills and curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, and at railroad crossings. In these areas, your view of oncoming traffic or trains is limited, making passing extremely dangerous. You must wait until you are in a clearly marked passing zone with good visibility.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, you should:
options: a:Wait for the police before moving the vehicle,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances,c:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway if it is safe to do so
note: After a minor collision, if your vehicle can be moved and no one has serious injuries, you should move it out of the travel lanes to reduce the risk of another crash. You must still stay at the scene, identify yourself, and provide any necessary help or information.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The right side of the road,b:The center of the road,c:Either side of the road
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge of the road or lane line as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you see enough of the roadway to stay in your lane safely.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: On a one-way street, when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must move as close as you safely can to the edge of the roadway and stop. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left but oncoming traffic is heavy, what should you do while the light is green?
options: a:Enter the intersection to prepare for the turn and wait for a safe gap,b:Wait in the crosswalk until traffic clears,c:Use the next intersection instead
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you may pull into the intersection to wait for a safe gap before turning left, as long as you do not block the crosswalk. When the light changes and oncoming traffic stops, you must clear the intersection by completing your turn if it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,c:Honk your horn at least three times.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors to see traffic behind you, signal your intention, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Only move into the passing lane when you are sure it is clear and legal, and return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means only the side with the broken line may pass. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass when traffic is clear and it is safe. Never pass if doing so would interfere with oncoming traffic or require you to exceed the speed limit.

question: How is driving much slower than the speed limit generally viewed?
options: a:It is always the safest option.,b:It always gives you the right-of-way.,c:It can be hazardous and you may need to let others pass.,d:You should never let following cars pass you.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can create a hazard because faster vehicles may need to brake or change lanes suddenly. On many two-lane roads, if several vehicles are stacked up behind you, you are required to pull over where safe and let them pass. Always travel at a speed that is safe for conditions and does not unnecessarily block traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.,d:The vehicle with faster speed.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there is no traffic control device.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A steady green left arrow gives you a protected left turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you are stopped, so you have the right-of-way to turn left. With a solid green light or flashing yellow arrow, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Ensure the lane you intend to use is clear before you move over,b:Always pass only on the right,c:Assume oncoming traffic will yield
note: On a multilane highway, always check that the lane you plan to move into is clear before changing lanes to pass. Use your mirrors, check blind spots, signal, and move over smoothly. Passing is usually done on the left; passing on the right is allowed only when it is legal and safe, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is enough room on the right.

question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and lights, what is true?
options: a:You must always follow it closely,b:You must yield the right-of-way to it,c:You may ignore it if you are in a hurry
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer or the emergency vehicle’s loudspeaker. Never follow an emergency vehicle closely or try to outrun it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,b:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,c:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right‑of‑way, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: A brake warning lamp on the instrument panel typically indicates:
options: a:The brake system may be defective if it illuminates while pressing the foot brake,b:It should come on when the parking brake is released,c:It will never come on
note: The brake warning light should come on briefly when you start the car and stay on while the parking brake is applied, then go off when the parking brake is fully released. If it comes on or stays on while you are driving or when you press the foot brake, it can indicate a serious brake system problem. In that case, you should not continue driving the vehicle until the brakes are checked.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,c:Release the gas and let the vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,d:All of the above.
note: To reduce the chance of being rear‑ended, avoid sudden, hard stops whenever possible, check your mirrors and blind spots before slowing or stopping, and ease off the accelerator so your brake lights come on gradually as you apply the brakes. These actions give drivers behind you more time to see you slowing and to react safely.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Turn your radio down to listen for a train,b:Proceed only when a flagger clears you,c:Approach cautiously and cross only after confirming no trains are coming
note: At a railroad crossing marked only with a crossbuck, you must approach slowly and be prepared to stop. Look and listen carefully in both directions for trains, and cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. If a flagger is present, you must obey their signals.

question: When sleet or snow begins, you should:
options: a:Drive at posted highway speeds without change,b:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance,c:Approach vehicles more closely to monitor them
note: In sleet or snow, traction is greatly reduced, so you must keep your windshield and mirrors clear for maximum visibility and increase your following distance to allow more time and space to stop safely.

question: When driving in fog, which actions should you take?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights for better illumination.,b:Drive cautiously, reduce speed, and use low beam headlights.,c:Turn off your headlights to avoid glare.,d:Speed up to leave the foggy area quickly.
note: In fog, slow down and drive cautiously while using low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the fog and create glare, making it harder to see, while low beams help you see the road and be seen by others.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, you should:
options: a:Assume someone may open a door and use extra caution,b:Speed up to pass quickly,c:Slam on your brakes
note: When passing a vehicle parked at the curb, always assume someone might open a door or step out. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be prepared to stop to avoid hitting an opening door or a pedestrian.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck sign is used at railroad crossings and acts like a yield sign. It warns you that you are at a railroad crossing and you must look and listen for trains and yield the right-of-way to any approaching train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane,b:Before entering the deceleration lane,c:Only after you see the toll booth
note: When exiting a highway, signal and move into the exit or deceleration lane first, then reduce your speed smoothly within that lane. Do not slow down sharply while still in the main travel lane, as this can surprise drivers behind you.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path, and stop when safe.,d:Speed up to get away from the emergency vehicle.
note: On a divided multilane highway, you must still yield to approaching emergency vehicles using lights or siren. Safely slow down, move to the side or another lane to create a clear path, and stop if needed so the emergency vehicle can pass. Do not speed up or ignore the signal.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to deter them.,d:Confront them by blocking their path.
note: When dealing with an aggressive driver, focus on safety and avoiding conflict. Safely move out of their way, allow them to pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures. Do not speed up, block them, or confront them, as this can escalate road rage and increase crash risk.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian by law.,b:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever started moving last.,d:Whoever is slower.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are lawfully crossing the street, including at intersections without traffic lights or marked crosswalks. When turning, slow down and be prepared to stop so pedestrians can cross safely before you complete your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, you should generally ____ your speed.
options: a:Maintain speed,b:Vary by slowing to maintain control,c:Increase speed
note: Before and during a turn, you should usually slow down enough to stay in full control of the vehicle. Enter the turn at a safe speed, maintain a steady speed through the turn, and then gently accelerate as you complete it. Turning too fast can cause you to skid or drift out of your lane.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Blow the horn repeatedly.,b:Slam on the brakes until it stops.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Turn off the ignition carefully, apply brakes, and steer to a safe area to stop.
note: If your accelerator sticks, shift to neutral if possible, then turn the ignition off only far enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Steer smoothly to the side of the road, apply the brakes firmly but smoothly, and stop in a safe place. Do not turn the key to the lock position while moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles to get out of your way.,b:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,c:Honk your horn to alert others.,d:Merge quickly without stopping if traffic looks light.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must come to a complete stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway. You must yield to all pedestrians on the sidewalk and to all vehicles already on the road, proceeding only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what sequence of looking should you use before proceeding?
options: a:Look right, then left, then right again.,b:Look left first, then right, then left again.,c:Only check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.,d:Wait for the car ahead to move before looking.
note: At a stop sign, after stopping completely, you should first look left (where the nearest cross traffic comes from), then right, then left again to double-check for any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians before proceeding.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing another vehicle illegal?
options: a:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is illegal in several situations, including on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, when it requires driving on the shoulder, or where solid pavement markings prohibit passing. If any of these conditions exist, you must not pass.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates:
options: a:Stop,b:Speed limit,c:Hospital ahead
note: Octagonal (eight-sided) signs are used exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which sections of road are most likely to freeze first in cold, wet weather?
options: a:Flat sections of roadway.,b:Shaded sections of roadway.,c:Roads that are in the sun.
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, bridges, or near buildings, freeze first because they stay colder and receive less sunlight. They also stay icy longer after temperatures rise, so you should be extra cautious when driving through shaded sections in cold, wet weather.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane until it passes.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.,d:Speed up and get out of its way by any lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, you must safely pull over to the right edge or curb of the road and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely through traffic.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving?
options: a:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications,b:Only illegal drugs,c:Only prescription drugs
note: Any drug that affects the brain or body can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Some can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment, so always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:May still turn in that direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:No longer may turn and must go straight,c:Keep the right-of-way to turn
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but when it changes to a solid green light, you lose that protection. You may still turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and only turn when it is safe.

question: Which of the following is least likely to occur after drinking?
options: a:Your judgment is distorted,b:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down,c:None of these — alcohol causes all of them
note: Alcohol affects many parts of your driving ability. It distorts your judgment, making you more likely to take risks, and it slows your reflexes and reaction time, making it harder to respond quickly to hazards. Because alcohol causes all of these effects, none of the listed changes is “least likely.”

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow roadway when meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road,b:Stop immediately and honk your horn,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over
note: On narrow roads, each vehicle should leave sufficient space; allow the other vehicle at least half the traveled portion to pass safely.

question: What minimum following interval should you leave behind the vehicle ahead?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:100 feet.,d:Five seconds.
note: To reduce the risk of rear-end collisions, leave at least a two-second following interval under normal driving conditions.

question: A vehicle using emergency signals is approaching from the opposite direction on a two-lane street. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard it because it is coming the other way.,b:Stop as quickly as you can in your lane.,c:Slow down, move as far to the right as possible, and stop.,d:Try to outrun it to clear the way.
note: On a two-lane street, slow down and pull as far right as possible and stop to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,b:Honk continuously to scare it off.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible to get by quickly.,d:Maintain speed and expect the animal to move.
note: Be very cautious around animals on the road. Slow down and pass slowly so you don't frighten or startle the animal.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:Have large blind spots.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop than passenger cars.

question: Orange traffic signs most commonly indicate what?
options: a:Regulatory requirements.,b:School zone areas.,c:Work zones and road construction ahead.,d:General information.
note: Orange signs with black symbols or letters typically warn of highway work zones and that people or equipment may be on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street unless you:
options: a:Are driving the fastest vehicle on the road,b:Can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic,c:Have the legal right to pass regardless of visibility
note: To pass safely on a two-lane road you must be able to see clearly ahead and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle and check before getting in to reverse,b:Only use rearview mirrors while reversing,c:Honk immediately before shifting into reverse
note: Before backing, exit and inspect behind your vehicle for children and objects; mirrors alone may not reveal all hazards.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires adjusting your driving.,b:You should slow down in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.,d:All of the above.
note: Sudden weather changes require adjustments: slow down in rain or fog and watch for other vehicles that may not slow appropriately.

question: If a trailer blocks your internal rearview mirror, what is required?
options: a:Install an outside mirror on the driver's side.,b:Install an outside mirror on the passenger side.,c:Add outside rearview mirrors on both sides of the towing vehicle.,d:Remove the trailer.
note: If a trailer obstructs the inside mirror, you must install properly sized outside rearview mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.

question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do to reduce crash risk?
options: a:Use alternate routes only.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time.,d:Brake harder to stop sooner.
note: On slippery roads increase your following distance because it takes longer to stop than under normal conditions.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke affect driving?
options: a:It does not affect driving ability.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity.,d:It improves focus on the road.
note: Smoking and handling smoking materials are distractions that can take your hands and eyes off driving tasks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign show?
options: a:Only a suggested driving speed.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:The one speed that prevents all crashes.,d:The maximum speed in poor weather.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. Slow down when conditions (weather, traffic) require it.

question: What driving practice helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Anticipating traffic and slowing gradually instead of braking and accelerating frequently reduces fuel consumption.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard,c:Assume the crossing guard may be ignored
note: Obey crossing guards and posted signs in school zones; be prepared to reduce speed and take extra care for children.

question: What name is given to signs that drivers must obey?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs are the signs that state laws and rules you must obey, such as speed limits, stop signs, and yield signs. Ignoring these signs can result in tickets or crashes because they control traffic movement and right-of-way.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:They are making quick and sudden stops.,d:Any of these behaviors can indicate an impaired driver.
note: Weaving between lanes is a classic sign of an impaired driver, but so are driving much slower than surrounding traffic and making quick, sudden stops. Any of these behaviors can indicate a drunk or otherwise impaired driver, and you should increase your following distance and report them if it is safe to do so.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, how should you prepare?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must slow down, look, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby, and never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates, because trains cannot stop quickly.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that workers may be present,b:That it is summer and paving season,c:You must immediately stop and back up
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work is ahead and conditions may be changing. You should slow down, be alert for workers and equipment near the roadway, and be prepared for lane shifts, reduced speeds, or stopped traffic.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop driving and rest,b:Open a window or get coffee and keep going,c:Turn up the radio volume
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; stop and rest or switch drivers rather than continuing while drowsy.

question: When driving on public streets or highways, you must:
options: a:Have and show your driver license to law enforcement upon request,b:Only have a license at home,c:Be able to recite your license number from memory
note: You must carry a valid driver license while operating a vehicle and present it to an officer when requested.

question: What is the best way to reduce your chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy,b:Watch out for standing water or puddles,c:Keep your tires properly maintained
note: To avoid hydroplaning, maintain proper tire condition and pressure, reduce speed in wet conditions, and avoid standing water when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right,b:The vehicle on the left,c:The larger vehicle
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: When are you allowed to go around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:After the lights stop flashing and the train has passed,c:When you hear the train but see no cars on the tracks
note: Never drive around lowered crossing gates; wait until signals indicate it is safe and the gates are fully raised.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When emergency vehicle sirens are heard, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow them to pass.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning, you should:
options: a:Maintain good tire tread and proper inflation and reduce speed in the rain,b:Only ensure tires are properly inflated,c:Only reduce speed when puddles appear
note: Good tread and correct tire pressure plus reducing speed in wet conditions greatly reduce hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:One driver may continue driving without stopping.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an open intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When changing lanes, how should you check blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to view the blind spot,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror,c:Rely solely on outside mirrors
note: A head check over the shoulder is required to confirm the blind spot is clear before a lane change.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on drivers?
options: a:It increases reflexes and reaction time.,b:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,c:It makes drivers more alert.,d:It only affects mood, not driving skills.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reduces reaction time, and impairs driving skills necessary for safe operation.

question: When you park facing downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,d:Turn your wheels toward the center of the road.
note: On a downhill slope, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road so that if your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the children.,b:Rev the engine briefly to gain attention.,c:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to ensure the way is clear.,d:Back out slowly while watching through the rearview mirror.
note: Before reversing where children may be present, get out and check behind the vehicle; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: A driver taking an over-the-counter (non-prescription) medication should:
options: a:Read labels and heed warnings before driving,b:Drink alcohol to offset drowsiness,c:Ignore labels and continue driving
note: Many OTC medications can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about driving while medicated.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Is never used as a traffic signal.,c:Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.
note: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light: traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.

question: If your car begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go,b:To keep the front wheels straight,c:In the opposite direction of the skid
note: Correct skid recovery is to steer into the direction you want the car to move until control returns, then straighten the wheel.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle trunk to improve traction.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.,d:Engage four-wheel drive and maintain normal following distances.
note: Reducing speed and increasing the distance between you and the vehicle ahead are the most important techniques for safe driving on snow or ice.

question: Which of the following may you legally install on your private vehicle?
options: a:A blue light visible outside of the vehicle.,b:A bell, exhaust whistle, or siren.,c:A muffler cut-out or by-pass.,d:None of the above.
note: It is illegal to add equipment such as exterior blue lights, bells/exhaust whistles/sirens, or muffler cut-outs that alter the vehicle's original safety equipment or mimic emergency vehicles.

question: Which traffic signal situation corresponds to stopping, yielding to cross traffic/pedestrians, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid green light
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,d:Recommended speeds only for novice drivers.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down for adverse conditions as necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As of 2026, what are the updated minimum liability auto insurance limits required in Hawaii?
note: Effective January 1, 2026, Hawaii increased its mandatory minimum liability limits to 40/80/20 ($40,000 bodily injury per person, $80,000 per accident, and $20,000 property damage).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Hawaii is a 'no-fault' insurance state. What is the mandatory minimum Personal Injury Protection (PIP) coverage required per person?
note: Hawaii requires all drivers to carry a minimum of $10,000 in Personal Injury Protection (PIP) coverage to cover medical expenses regardless of who is at fault.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Hawaii's Child Passenger Safety law, children under what age must be properly secured in a car seat or booster seat unless they are over 4 feet 9 inches tall?
options: a:Under 6 years old,b:Under 8 years old,c:Under 10 years old,d:Under 12 years old
note: Hawaii law requires children under 10 years of age to be properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or booster seat, unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Hawaii County Civil Defense and DMV guidelines, if you encounter lava crossing a road or a lava flow warning zone, what should you do?
options: a:Drive over the crust if it looks hardened,b:Turn around immediately — lava zones are extremely hazardous and roads may hide hollow or active lava beneath,c:Speed up to cross the area quickly,d:Wait in your car on the roadside
note: Active or recent lava flows are extremely unstable, can collapse, and release toxic gases. You must turn around immediately and respect all civil defense road closures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Hawaii law, what is the property damage threshold above which an accident must be reported to the police immediately?
options: a:$500 or more,b:$1,000 or more,c:$3,000 or more,d:$5,000 or more
note: Hawaii law requires any traffic crash resulting in apparent property damage of $3,000 or more, or any injury or death, to be reported to the police immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about how the Hawaii DMV tracks traffic convictions and violations?
options: a:Hawaii uses a standard 12-point demerit system,b:Hawaii uses a 24-point demerit system,c:Hawaii does not use a demerit point system,d:Hawaii removes all violations after 6 months
note: Hawaii does not use a demerit point system. Instead, traffic violations are kept on your record and the court or DMV suspends/revokes licenses based on specific offenses or numbers of convictions.
